title: The darkness is not dark (Psalm 139:11–12)
hookLine: the night shines as the day to you

lines: AN OLD SONG ABOUT THE DARK.
cards: The power goes out. The fridge stops humming, the screens die, and the room you know by heart becomes a room you don't. You reach for the wall.
A chair leg finds your shin. An old song goes right into that moment, and further, into the other kinds of dark: the sleepless hours before dawn, the year nobody could see the way through.
It's a psalm whose heading names David, and in the middle of it the singer says something strange about the dark.

teach.b: Psalm 139 starts with being known: "O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me." Then it turns into a kind of hide and seek, and the singer tries every hiding place.

teach.h: HEAVEN, THE DEPTHS, THE FAR SEA.
teach.b: "If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there." Up, down. Then the wings of the morning, the uttermost parts of the sea.
Even there. And then the last hiding place, the dark.

teach.h: THE DARKNESS HIDETH NOT FROM THEE.
teach.b: In the King James words: "If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee."
Readers hear the singer two ways here. Some hear someone hoping the dark will hide them. Others hear someone afraid it will swallow them whole.
Notice where the light comes from. No dawn arrives, no lamp is lit. The night is light about the singer because the night isn't dark to God, who sees in it as in the day.

teach.h: MADE IN SECRET, IN THE DARK.
teach.b: A few lines later the psalm goes to one more dark place, the womb, where, it says, I was made in secret. The singer's life began in the dark, and God was there too.
So for those who pray this psalm, the dark may still be dark. But it isn't empty.

how: Christians pray Psalm 139 in personal prayer and in worship, and in churches that pray night prayer, evening psalms and prayers ask for God's presence through the dark hours.

games.q: what does “the darkness is not dark” mean?
o: the psalm's trust that no night hides anyone from God
a warning that the dark is one place God cannot see
a saying that sadness is only in your imagination

games.q: the darkness is not dark — tap the pairs.
p: if I ascend up into heaven
the uttermost parts of the sea
even there shall thy hand lead me

s: in Psalm 139, the singer finds one hiding place God can't see: the dark
"the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day."
the psalm tries hiding places in heaven, in the depths and across the sea
heaven, the depths, the wings of the morning, the uttermost parts of the sea.
Psalm 139 begins with being searched and known
"O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me."

games.q: you're the singer of Psalm 139. you've tried heaven, the depths, and the far side of the sea, and God is there each time. one hiding place is left. what do you try?
o: a crowd, where nobody notices you.
the darkness: surely it shall cover me.
games.why: "surely the darkness shall cover me." and it doesn't: "the darkness and the light are both alike to thee."

practice: Dim the lights or close your eyes, and let the dark be what it is, the sounds that get louder, the edges that disappear; if something in your life feels dark right now, let it come in too, without fixing it.
If you pray, say the psalm's line slowly, the darkness and the light are both alike to thee; if not, simply rest here.
If the dark ever feels like too much to carry alone, or you're thinking of harming yourself, please call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: The darkness is not dark. Psalm 139's claim that there is no hiding place from God, not even the night, because the night shineth as the day.

orig.note: Hebrew: darkness, the word in Psalm 139:11–12.

carryVoice: Your line: dark and light alike. To God, the night shineth as the day. Until tomorrow.
